crisis.body: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in Sub-Saharan Africa, yet for many, it's detected far too late. Rural clinics lack the tools. Trained specialists are few. And treatment often comes too late.

mission.title: Designed for Frontline Care
mission.lead: IntelliBra empowers early breast cancer detection in even the most underserved communities by putting AI-assisted diagnostics in the hands of frontline clinicians.
mission.earlyDetectionBody: By identifying breast cancer at its earliest stages, IntelliBra dramatically improves treatment outcomes and long-term survival chances for women.
mission.realWorldBody: Every element of the IntelliBra device is purpose-built — from its portable hardware and integrated AI core to its seamless Bluetooth connectivity.
mission.cliniciansBody: IntelliBra equips nurses and general practitioners with intuitive, AI-assisted breast health screening tools to reduce reliance on specialists, and enable confident decision-making at the point of care.

app.body: With the IntelliBra Pink Alert app, patients can easily register, receive screening results, and manage follow-up care—all from their phone. It's secure, bilingual (English & French), and designed for ease of use, even with limited internet.

hero.headline: Building connected cancer care for every woman in Cameroon
hero.lead: IntelliBra combines portable AI-powered hardware, a guided clinician app, and a diagnostic engine trained on local patient data to bring early breast cancer detection to frontline clinics.

device.body: The IntelliBra device combines ultrasound and thermography to capture breast tissue data without radiation, pain, or invasive procedures. Designed for frontline use, it's handheld, lightweight, battery-powered, and functional in both hospital and outreach settings.

tabletApp.title: Tablet App That Guides and Records
tabletApp.lead: The IntelliBra tablet interface walks clinicians through screening step-by-step.
features: Store and sync records securely (even offline)

ai.body: IntelliBra's diagnostic engine uses a deep-learning model trained on real patient data from Sub-Saharan Africa, ensuring culturally and clinically relevant accuracy. The AI provides immediate classification during the scan and improves over time through ethical data feedback.

privacy.title: Privacy-Protected, Ethically Trained AI
privacy.lead: All IntelliBra data is anonymized, encrypted, and never used without consent, under the oversight of medical ethics boards.

steps.title: Frontline Screening Begins Here
steps.text: A trained clinician performs the screening using IntelliBra. Both ultrasound and thermography data are captured directly on the tablet alongside basic patient details. This is the only stage where patient identifiers exist.

steps.title: Protected, Even Offline
steps.text: Scan data is encrypted and saved securely on the device. Access requires authentication, and no external connection is needed. Devices operate offline and sync securely when internet access is available.

steps.title: Only With Your Consent
steps.text: If the patient consents, de-identified scan data (no names, no IDs) may be used to improve IntelliBra's diagnostic engine. Our AI learns and gets smarter, without compromising privacy.

hero.lead: IntelliBra is being evaluated across Cameroon to learn how portable, AI-assisted screening can help frontline clinicians detect breast cancer earlier. The study will welcome 2,840 women aged 25 and above, with every examination provided free of charge.
hero.imageAlt: A clinician using a tablet in a hospital

about.title: About the study
about.lead: A rigorous multicenter evaluation of AI-powered breast cancer screening across all 10 regions of Cameroon

cards.title: The device
cards.body: IntelliBra is a connected brassiere integrating miniaturized ultrasound sensors and infrared thermography, analyzed by an embedded AI algorithm in real time. It connects to a mobile application that transmits results to the Cameroon National Breast Cancer Registry (CNBCR).

cards.title: The comparison
cards.body: Results are compared against the standard reference examination: breast ultrasound for women under 40 and digital mammography for women aged 40 and above. In cases of suspected abnormality, biopsy serves as the definitive reference standard.

cards.title: Primary outcome
cards.body: The primary aim is to measure the sensitivity and specificity of IntelliBra versus the reference standard. Secondary outcomes include PPV, NPV, AUC, patient acceptability, ease of use, and early detection rate.

cards.title: Data and privacy
cards.body: All participant data is anonymized and stored in the CNBCR. No national identity number is collected. Data is accessible only to authorized researchers and shared upon formal request with ethical approval.

timeline.title: Study timeline
timeline.lead: A phased approach to rigorous clinical validation

phases.title: Preparation
phases.body: Formation of research team, ethics submission to CNERSH, regulatory filing with Cameroon health authorities, equipment deployment across 20 sites, staff training. Self-financed by ANORA S.A.S.

phases.title: Pilot
phases.body: Initial testing of study procedures and protocols before full-scale deployment. Feasibility and protocol validation. Results used to confirm readiness for expansion.

phases.title: Extension
phases.body: Validation of Phase I results on a broader sample. Comparative analysis between phases. Funding secured through fundraising based on Phase I outcomes.

phases.title: Full deployment
phases.body: Complete multicenter study across all 10 regions. Final statistical analysis including sensitivity, specificity, AUC, PPV, NPV, and acceptability metrics. Submission for peer-reviewed publication.

phases.title: Results publication
phases.body: Summary results published in the PACTR registry and submitted to peer-reviewed journals per WHO requirements. Data made available via the CNBCR platform for qualified secondary research.

eligibility.title: Who can participate
eligibility.lead: Screening is free. Participation is voluntary, and you can leave the study at any time.
eligibility.reviewLabel: Talk with the study team first if
essential: You are a woman aged 25 or older
You live near a participating study center
You can give consent and attend follow-up if needed
review: You are receiving active breast cancer treatment
You recently had major or invasive breast surgery
eligibility.clinicianNote: A study clinician will confirm final eligibility and answer your questions.
inclusion: Residing in areas covered by participating study centers
Voluntarily agreed to participate after receiving full informed consent
Available for follow-up examinations at 6 and 12 months if required
Women with or without prior history of breast disease or risk factors
exclusion: Confirmed pregnancy at the time of enrollment
History of major breast surgery that altered breast morphology
Serious unstabilized medical condition preventing safe participation
Currently undergoing active treatment for breast cancer
Invasive breast procedure within 6 months prior to enrollment
Refusal to sign the informed consent form
